financials_interim.notes: Company-basis (standalone, ex-Singer Finance (Lanka) PLC subsidiary) column of the same filing; no 'Direct Interest Cost' line here since the finance company is not consolidated at this level. short_term_borrowings = Interest-Bearing Loans and Borrowings current (35,810,552) + Bank Overdrafts (2,524,082); long_term_borrowings = Interest-Bearing Loans and Borrowings non-current (4,224,500). EPS check: 1,915,089k / 1,167,617,912 shares = Rs.1.640 ~= stated 1.64, ties out cleanly.

cost_of_sales is Cost of Sales (23,932,189) plus Direct Interest Cost (2,373,301) = 26,305,490; the P&L presents 'Direct Interest Cost' (the funding cost of the Financial Services/Singer Finance (Lanka) PLC lending book) as a separate line between Cost of Sales and Gross Profit, so it has been folded into cost_of_sales here so that Revenue - cost_of_sales = Gross Profit (38,722,928-26,305,490=12,417,438, ties to stated Gross Profit). Group Trade and Other Receivables also has a non-current component of 32,036,832 (mostly Singer Finance's longer-tenor lease/loan receivables) in addition to the 94,230,838 current balance recorded in trade_receivables here -- only the current-asset figure is captured in this field to stay consistent with current_assets. short_term_borrowings/long_term_borrowings include only genuine interest-bearing debt (Interest-Bearing Loans and Borrowings + Bank Overdrafts); 'Other Financial Liabilities' (current Rs.28,865,658 / non-current Rs.16,986,318) were deliberately EXCLUDED as these are believed to be Singer Finance (Lanka) PLC's customer deposit liabilities (the cash flow statement shows an 'Increase in Customer Deposit Liabilities' of Rs.4,573,443k for the quarter, which is of a similar order of magnitude), per the project convention of never treating customer deposits as borrowings. EPS check: attributable profit 2,147,610k / 1,167,617,912 shares = Rs.1.839 ~= stated 1.84; ties out cleanly, no column-swap ambiguity in this filing.

interim_updates.note_text: SINS Group revenue grew 41% YoY to Rs.38,722.9Mn (Q1 FY25/26: Rs.27,552.8Mn), with every segment up: Home Appliances, the largest, rose 39.0% to Rs.13,602.9Mn; Financial Services (Singer Finance (Lanka) PLC) grew 49.6% to Rs.7,184.0Mn; Digital Products grew 20.4% to Rs.6,926.4Mn; and Automobile and Other nearly 2.5x'd from Rs.1,891.0Mn to Rs.4,715.8Mn. Operating profit grew even faster, +59.4% to Rs.4,800.4Mn, led by Automobile and Other PBT contribution rising from Rs.76.0Mn to Rs.293.2Mn (+285.6%), Digital Products PBT +74.1% to Rs.510.0Mn, and Home Appliances PBT +60.2% to Rs.1,565.9Mn; Financial Services remained the single largest PBT contributor by segment at Rs.1,925.5Mn (+56.4% YoY). Below the operating line, net finance cost more than doubled, from Rs.437.3Mn to Rs.971.8Mn (+122%), as Finance Cost rose to Rs.1,207.2Mn (from Rs.786.0Mn) while Finance Income fell to Rs.235.4Mn (from Rs.348.8Mn) -- reflecting both a larger consolidated debt/deposit base (interest-bearing borrowings up from Rs.55.3Bn to Rs.80.3Bn since 30 June 2025) and higher funding costs on the Singer Finance book; VAT on Financial Services also rose from Rs.239.3Mn to Rs.354.3Mn in line with the growth in financial-services income. Even after absorbing both of these, PBT still grew 48.8% to Rs.3,474.3Mn and PAT 44.3% to Rs.2,241.1Mn (attributable-to-owners profit +43.9% to Rs.2,147.6Mn), with Basic/Diluted EPS up from Rs.1.28 to Rs.1.84. Working-capital investment to support this growth pushed net operating cash flow to -Rs.4,099.1Mn (still negative, though better than -Rs.5,175.9Mn a year earlier), driven by a Rs.6,069.6Mn increase in debtors falling due within one year and a Rs.1,500.2Mn increase in longer-dated debtors, partly offset by a Rs.527.4Mn inventory release.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one has been collected for SINS -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. Note this filing's Statement of Financial Position uniquely provides a true same-quarter-last-year comparative (30 June 2025) in addition to the prior fiscal year-end (31 March 2026) -- unlike a typical LKAS 34 filing that only compares to FYE -- but only the current 30 June 2026 balance-sheet figures are stored in this row; the 30 June 2025 balance-sheet column was not separately entered as a historical row. short_term_borrowings/long_term_borrowings deliberately exclude 'Other Financial Liabilities' on the Group balance sheet (current Rs.28,865,658k / non-current Rs.16,986,318k) as these are believed to represent Singer Finance (Lanka) PLC's customer deposit liabilities, not interest-bearing debt -- see notes field on the GROUP financial_statements row.
interim_updates.takeaway: Headline growth (revenue +41%, PBT +49%, PAT +44%) is broad-based across segments and not a one-off, but it is being funded aggressively -- net finance cost more than doubled YoY and operating cash flow remains negative (-Rs.4.1Bn) as receivables and the lending book continue to expand faster than collections, so the quality of this growth depends on the Financial Services book's credit performance and SINS's ability to keep refinancing a fast-growing, largely short-term-funded balance sheet.
operational_highlights: Group revenue Rs.38,722.9Mn, up 41% YoY; broad-based across all seven segments (Home Appliances +39.0%, Financial Services +49.6%, Automobile & Other +149.4%).
Group Operating Profit Rs.4,800.4Mn (+59.4% YoY); Group PBT Rs.3,474.3Mn (+48.8%); Group PAT Rs.2,241.1Mn (+44.3%).
Basic/Diluted EPS Rs.1.84 vs Rs.1.28 a year earlier (+43.8%).
Net Finance Cost more than doubled to Rs.971.8Mn (from Rs.437.3Mn) as Finance Cost rose to Rs.1,207.2Mn and Finance Income fell to Rs.235.4Mn.
Net operating cash outflow of Rs.4,099.1Mn (vs -Rs.5,175.9Mn prior year), driven by a Rs.6,069.6Mn build in short-term trade receivables.

First interim dividend of Rs.0.50/share (Rs.583.8Mn) declared 30 June 2026, paid 22 July 2026; Board also approved a Rs.630Mn Piliyandala property acquisition (completed 24 July 2026, after period end).
key_drivers: Financial Services segment (Singer Finance (Lanka) PLC) remains the largest PBT contributor, Rs.1,925.5Mn (+56.4% YoY), but is also the source of the funding-cost pressure dragging on net finance cost.
Automobile and Other segment PBT nearly quadrupled YoY (Rs.76.0Mn to Rs.293.2Mn), the fastest-growing contributor in percentage terms.

Net Finance Cost swing (-Rs.534.6Mn YoY) is the single biggest drag between Operating Profit and PBT, on the back of a larger consolidated borrowings base (Group interest-bearing loans/borrowings + overdrafts up from ~Rs.57.3Bn to ~Rs.84.2Bn between 30 June 2025 and 30 June 2026) and lower finance income.
Impairment Loss on Trade and Other Receivables rose to Rs.187.3Mn from Rs.120.3Mn, tracking the growth in the receivables book.

_gaps: ebitda: depreciation_amortization not disclosed; EBITDA understated (= operating profit only)
